data.name: Jood
data.gender_notes: Jood is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'jawwad' which means grapes or fruit in general. The name Jood is also mentioned in the Quran and is associated with Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). The name Jood carries the meaning “Grapes” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Jood usually hope their child will grow to embody grapes and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Jood belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Grapes.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jood total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_arabic.name: جود

in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم جود مشتق من جود و هو يعني الكرم و السخاء و العطاء بدون انتظار مقابل، ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قول الله تعالى: 'وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ'، و جود هو من الأسماء التي تحمل معاني جميلة و محمودة في الإسلام

This time symbolizes the harvest season and the fruitfulness of life. It may also have associations with aspects of Islamic art and culture involving vine motifs and grape designs, as seen in various Islamic architectural elements and intricate decorative patterns.
